== Biography ==
Andrew Glasgow, Esq., is described in the held account as of Deanfoot, Peeblesshire, with a reported death in 1819. His birth estimate about 1760 and the more specific November 1819 death field remain uncertain. <ref>https://archive.org/details/sim_blackwoods-magazine_1819-10_6_31/page/120/mode/2up?q=%22Andrew+Glasgow%22</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Earlier vital wording retained ===

The earlier account stated: “Andrew Glasgow, Esq. of Deanfoot, Peebleshire who died in 1819.” That is retained as a reported claim from the existing Blackwood’s citation, not a death fact independently established by the baptism indexes. Neither the estimated birth about 1760 nor the current uncertain November 1819 field is replaced here.

=== Possible childhood: Kirknewton baptism, 1750 ===

A newly inspected OPR derivative records an unnamed Glasgow child baptised on 6 May 1750 at Kirknewton and East Calder, with father Andrew Glasgow and mother Isabel. It supplies neither the child's first name nor the mother's surname. The reference is OPR 690/2, item 2.<ref name="Kirknewton1750Detailed">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births &amp; Baptisms 1564–1929'', [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4476061 SCOT/OPR/BAP/4476061], baptism 6 May 1750, Kirknewton &amp; East Calder, Midlothian, OPR 690/2, item 2, register range 1642–1764. Child's first name “-”; father Andrew Glasgow; mother's first name Isabel, no maternal surname field. Derivative transcript inspected 4 November 2026; original register uninspected.</ref>

Two already-held companion indexes name the child Andrew Glasgow and give his parents as Andrew Glasgow and Isabel Clerk, with the same exact baptism day and parish.<ref name="Kirknewton1750Named">Findmypast, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_686207645&tab=this R_686207645] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_691904464&tab=this R_691904464], ''Scotland, Parish Births &amp; Baptisms 1564–1929'', Andrew Glasgow, baptism 6 May 1750, Kirknewton and East Calder, father Andrew Glasgow and mother Isabel Clerk. Saved labelled derivatives inspected 22 October 2026; original register uninspected. R_686207645 additionally records Kirknewton residence.</ref> These matching fields identify the same held record event. Andrew's name and the maternal surname Clerk come from those named companions, not from the newly recovered detailed fields. The three derivatives are not independent witnesses, and their indexed birth year does not establish an exact birthday.

Andrew of Deanfoot remains only a weak compatible identification for that child. His current estimated birth about 1760 differs from the baptism generation by about ten years, but the estimate is not an independently proved exclusion. No inspected family, estate, occupation or residence evidence connects the 1750 child to the later Deanfoot adult. The existing death account and the separate initial-only 1794 shipping comparison do not supply that connection. No baptism or birth is assigned to this profile.

The existing [[Glasgow-1336|Andrew Glasgow]] and [[Clerk-314|Isobel Clerk]] household is a possible comparison for the recorded parents, separate from identifying this child with the Deanfoot adult. Neither named adult profile is established by the new receipt, and Isabel's surname Clerk is supported only by the held named companions. No father, mother, spouse, sibling or other relative is attached; all current fields and assessments remain unchanged. The original parish entry and an independent Deanfoot family or estate record are the useful next tests.


=== Possible A. Glascow, 1794 arrival ===
A. Glascow from Glasgow is named with H. Jurriens from Riga and J. Mark from Königsbergen in a shipping-arrival report for 24 June 1794, under the Rotterdam dateline of 25 June.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1335425007/ Rotterdamse courant, 26 June 1794, p.2].</ref>

Only the initial A. is given. The list probably names a shipmaster, but it does not state a vessel, full forename, sex, family or personal origin. Glasgow is the departure port. P. L. Markwaarden in the following entry is a different person.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3165]]. Chronologically adult in 1794, with a later reported Scottish death. The known account cites an October 1819 Blackwood’s Magazine result but supplies no occupation or event connection. The title ‘Esq’ is not maritime evidence.
